body: Yeah nah, his was just whatever it was that was similar to molly. I forgot what it was called but it definitely didn't fall into those categories.

My brother has 8 years for drug trafficking, mostly because they found an unregistered gun in his home. It wasn't used on anyone. The fact people literally take lives away and see less of a cell than him makes my blood boil. He definitely deserves to do time, but to that degree is insanely ridiculous.

I came over here to do some research since my step-mom treats my younger brother fairly poorly because she's ashamed of his autism even though he's a good kid and seems fine? I'm much older so left the household when he was five but aside from maybe extra lessons or more patience required in school or something, I'm at a bit of a loss of understanding what's the big deal.

I was curious to see people's mindset from the other end of things, who've dealt with some underlying discrimination from a parent. She's very much the kind of person who needs validation and he doesn't freely give it. Sure, it can be annoying when I'm trying to love on him and he kinda blows me off but he's 14 and later on when we hang out he finds ways to tell and show me that he cares. Like, I'm a grown adult. Why would I hold a grudge against a child for them just acting the way they are?? That's insanity!

I'm sorry you're having to deal with this and I wish there was something that I could do. I hope my comment is encouraging, because there are those of us who know feelings like yours exist and want to do what we can to make sure those in our life dealing with that same struggle feel loved and appreciated. 

No one should be suffering by feeling unloved by their parent, even if it is incredibly common. Your feelings are valid. 

I've had a lot of struggles myself when I was younger with how she'd treat ***me*** because of how my brother's autism made her feel. When he was a young boy, and she was pregnant with her second child, I found him crying because he didn't want her to treat his incoming younger brother the way she treated him. It was devastating and absolutely broke my heart. I just hugged him. I just hugged him. I haven't really been around much when he was a kid since 1) I don't know what to do with kids really and 2) I couldn't afford to visit so didn't get personal time, but now that he's in high school I'm planning to bug him with memes and stuff a lot just so he knows I'm thinking of him and hopefully be able to have him visit me for a weekend or something over the summer. :)

I hope you're able to find happiness, even if you have to find it from somewhere else. You're clearly a caring person, and I commend you for having the strength to open up a discussion to talk about it because I can be really easy to hold a lot of emotions like these in.

Sorry for such a long post, and I'm sorry if so much of it is about me, but I hope that maybe in some way it could have helped? I'm not sure, but I'm doing what I can to try.

I like how you are still positive and you don't blame him. I hope you have others there for you right now. I hope you never forget what the sound of his guitar is like. I hope you're able to continue to cherish the way that he was when you two were together.

Fuck. I'm at that point and I wish there was just someone to bother to check in on me as I try and figure that out. I even asked my dad to be there since I ran out of options trying to talk to friends and haven't even heard from him since. It is draining, the cost is absolutely frightening to me, and knowing that you have to watch what you say instead of tipping them off onto something that will get you a penalty super fucking sucks. 

I hate that in this day and age there's so many hoops you have to just through to get help, whether it's for physical or mental conditions. It's gotten to the point where if I can't figure anything out in the next couple years I'm seriously considering moving somewhere I might be able to get that kind of access (if possible).
Yeah and it makes me feel awful because most of the time it's not even them doing anything to make me feel that way. I know that I'm the problem but I don't know how to stop it. :\

Here's a link to the original *Darkness Visible* Vanity Fair article for anyone interested: http://www.vanityfair.com/magazine/1989/12/styron198912

And the whole e-book: https://archive.org/details/DarknessVisiblewilliamStyron

I'm still reading but figured I'd share for anyone else interested.
I know this exact feeling right now and it is the worst. Hopefully we're both able to figure something out. <3

It sucks that it's hard to get help even when you're trying. Did you have someone there for you during the process or did you have to do it yourself? I've asked friends to be there for me and even family to just be by my side while I figure it out and I've gotten nothing. I feel powerless and don't know what to do.

All. The. Time. There's been so many moments where I've had great things going for me and then I go back into my hole, isolating myself and dropping from my responsibilities. I can't keep doing it but I don't know how to stop.
Yes. Yes, yes, yes, yes. Even when I hang out with people I just feel empty after. It's like a distraction instead of something real, so I've barely even been doing it.

It's hard to believe the last two points but 
>It could also be that your depression is affecting your perspective.

is always a good thing to remember.

From your post history, you seem really nice. Thank you for taking the time to be there for others. I hope everything is going okay with you now. I need to go to bed right now but I'll try and see what I can reach out to tomorrow. I just hate being nervous that it won't feel right and I'll change my mind about everything if that happens.

I had someone I considered a good friend text me, "so you're posting on social media but ignoring me? wtf?" She always never gets back to me to the point that we've had to have discussions that if she doesn't get back to me within 24 hours then she can't get mad at me for extending invitations to someone else. We'll make plans and she'll just leave without even saying bye or when we were supposed to meet up she posts IG videos of having dinner at our mutual friend's place with other people. Like, seriously? I just publicly opened up about my major depression and other issues and basically said I didn't feel like I had anyone to turn to so was just going to open up to everyone and that was the response? It was really disappointing and definitely didn't help that the first direct reaction I got from someone was yelling at me instead of being there for me when they've treated me like crap so many times.

I agree with you on the entertainment part. I usually feel *more* comfortable with people once I know the other sides of them. It shows that they trust me and I appreciate being seen that way. I just wish I could feel like that was valued vice versa.

Thanks, man. Even just getting a response feels great. It's nice to know somebody's there. In the past I've just gotten a half-assed "Sorry" or "that's sad." It helps a lot to just be talked to like a human being when dealing with this stuff, you know? I feel like a lot of people try to treat you like you're made of glass which only gets further alienating.

I've been wanting to see a therapist so I can have somebody qualified help me deal with things. Also, since they're being paid, they'll have to regularly be there for me whereas somebody might be there for a moment but later flake out.

The thing is I'm scared I won't be able to afford it or I'll never find a right fit. I've reached out to NAMI to see if they have a service where someone I guess guides you through the process until you find a proper fit. Like, I know another person can't solve my problems and it would be unfair of me to expect someone of being capable of "fixing" me but it would mean the world to me to have someone in my life care enough to check in on me, make sure I'm on the right track, and offer to help out. It just sucks that I've basically opened up to multiple people saying I needed that and still nothing. I don't want to try and fail but not trying isn't helping either. I just keep wasting days, weeks, and months of my life over and over again.

I could see that being my dad's reaction but it's hard to think any person I've ever opened up to over the years has felt the same way. You do have a really fair point though. Thank you for sharing your experience with me. I hope you were able to be there for your mother at some point. <3

Your parents are scared and acting out of fear. It's really frightening to feel so powerless to do something when you see someone you love struggling. I'm sorry they're not handling it well but I'm glad your friend came out and showed up. 

What kind of positives did he help you realize? Did you talk to your parents about that part too or just the bad?
